description: A passionate team of students united by curiosity, innovation, and a shared interest in space and science. We work together to turn creative ideas into solutions that can make a difference.
summary:
We built a Godot 4 game hub that turns simplified astronaut mission concepts into playable training exercises. Players start in a 3D space hangar and choose a mission from a simple selector. There are two missions so far. In Lunar Lander, a 2D challenge, players control thrust and rotation and must manage limited fuel to touch down gently on scoring pads. In Robo-Arm, a 3D simulator, players coordinate four joints and a gripper to grab cargo and place it precisely in a drop zone, like the robotic arms used on space stations.

The project addresses the challenge by making space operations hands-on. Instead of reading about landings and robotic manipulation, players feel the trade-offs of fuel, gravity, coordination, and precision. Scores, timers, and instant restarts encourage repeated practice (the controls are explained in detail in the settings tab).

It matters because space and STEM topics can feel distant, and short, accessible games lower the barrier to curiosity. The modular menu means a new mission is added with a single entry, so the project can grow into a larger educational platform.
details:
The Concept & Inspiration

Named after astronomer Johannes Kepler—whose laws of planetary motion govern every spacecraft trajectory and orbital transfer today—Kepler's Cadet places players inside a virtual space academy to complete practical flight simulations. Space exploration relies on razor-thin margins of error, yet the engineering behind it can feel intimidating to newcomers. Our goal was to distill real NASA mission techniques into lighthearted, skill-based mini-games that anyone can pick up and enjoy.Gameplay & Real NASA Science

Greeted on the main menu by our custom 3D robot mascot—whose eyes interactively track the player's cursor across the screen—cadets take on two distinct space-operations challenges:Mini-Game 1: Lunar Precision Landing — Inspired by NASA’s Apollo and Artemis lunar descent maneuvers, players must carefully balance thruster propulsion, alignment, and gravitational pull to touch down safely inside a designated green landing zone on the Moon's surface—turning physics calculations into a tense, funny balancing act.Mini-Game 2: Orbital Robotic Cargo Control — Inspired by the International Space Station’s Canadarm2 and commercial resupply missions, players pilot an articulated robotic arm in microgravity to grab floating food and supply crates and slot them accurately into their designated storage bays.How We Built It

Developed as a two-person student team under a tight hackathon sprint, Kepler's Cadet combines physics simulation with playful UI interaction:Game Engine & Logic: Built in Godot, featuring custom gravity, thrust, and collision mechanics for lunar descent, articulated joint controls for zero-G cargo handling, and real-time cursor-tracking eye animations on the main menu.Custom 3D Mascot & Branding: We modeled and textured our original 3D robot character, integrating it both as an interactive menu companion and as the centerpiece of our game's emblem. Audio & Atmosphere: Immersive space-themed background music and sound effects (sourced from royalty-free sound libraries) bring tactile feedback to every thruster burn and robotic grab.Future Vision

Our mini-game hub is designed to expand. Beyond lunar landings and robotic cargo handling, future updates will introduce additional space-engineering modules, including orbital debris cleanup and solar array alignment.
